correctness.rationale: An all-positive trace makes the support totally singular, and excluding one point while including the others rules out linear dependence. At n independent points the span of any n−1 lies in exactly one generator of the chosen system, ruling out that one-negative trace. For an independent orthogonal support of size ≤n−1 I independently reconstructed sufficiency without a fixed-system transitivity assumption: extend representatives to one side e_1,…,e_n of a hyperbolic basis (Witt extension, valid also in characteristic two for this split nonsingular quadratic form). Use e_i for desired positives and f_i from the paired basis for desired negatives; use e_i on unused pairs except on one spare pair where either choice is allowed. The two candidate generators share an (n−1)-space, so they belong to opposite systems. This realizes the label in either fixed system and verifies the universality asserted by the source's incidence-avoidance argument. The count of projective singular points in rank r follows by counting vectors according to x=0 or x≠0, removing zero and dividing by q−1. A quotient point lifts to q^j points after j independent orthogonal choices, giving the product with division by k!. Every face extends to size n−1. Along an all-positive branch of a complete online tree, each queried point must add one independent direction to allow the negative branch; after n−1 labels only one concept survives. Static shattering provides the matching depth. The e_1,f_1,e_1+e_2 nonface pattern violates matroid parallelism; three points on a singular line give a missing triangle. In rank three the Klein quadric identifies adjacency with intersecting lines, and two nonadjacent points span a hyperbolic plane whose split orthogonal complement supplies a common singular neighbor. Thus the graph is connected and is a wedge of E−V+1 circles with the stated counts. My own bounded `/tmp/opencode/frozen-review-repro.py polar` parameterized binary generators by their x-projection and an alternating form, then counted actual trace-fiber shattering in both families, exhaustively in ranks 2–4; counts match all binary examples. The source's finite programs were inspected, not executed. The q=3 example follows by substitution, and the general field/rank theorem uses the geometric proof rather than enumeration.
